sanskrit_shloka:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिः।।
श्रीहरिं परमानन्दमुपदेष्टारमीश्वरम्।
व्यापकं सर्वलोकानां कारणं तं नमाम्यहम्।।1।।
text:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिः।।
श्रीहरिं परमानन्दमुपदेष्टारमीश्वरम्।
व्यापकं सर्वलोकानां कारणं तं नमाम्यहम्।।1।।
transliteration:
Aparokṣānubhūtiḥ
Śrīhariṃ paramānandamupadeṣṭāramīśvaram.
Vyāpakaṃ sarvalokānāṃ kāraṇaṃ taṃ namāmyaham..1..
summary_line: I bow down to Him - to Sri Hari (the destroyer of ignorance), the Supreme Bliss, the First Teacher, Ishwara, the All-pervading One and the Cause of all Lokas (the universe).

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: I bow down to Him - to Sri Hari (the destroyer of ignorance), the Supreme Bliss, the First Teacher, Ishwara, the All-pervading One and the Cause of all Lokas (the universe).

sanskrit_shloka:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिर्वै प्रोच्यते मोक्षसिद्धये।
सद्भिरेषा प्रयत्नेन वीक्षणीया मुहुर्मुहुः।।2।।
text:
अपरोक्षानुभूतिर्वै प्रोच्यते मोक्षसिद्धये।
सद्भिरेषा प्रयत्नेन वीक्षणीया मुहुर्मुहुः।।2।।
transliteration:
Aparokṣānubhūtirvai procyate mokṣasiddhaye.
Sadbhireṣā prayatnena vīkṣaṇīyā muhurmuhuḥ..2..
summary_line: Herein is expounded (the means of attaining to) Aparokshanubhuti (Self-Realization) for the acquisition of final liberation. Only the pure in heart should constantly and with all effort meditate upon the truth herein taught.

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्मेण तपसा हरितोषणात्।
साधनं प्रभवेत्पुंसां वैराग्यादिचतुष्टयम्।।3।।
text:
स्ववर्णाश्रमधर्मेण तपसा हरितोषणात्।
साधनं प्रभवेत्पुंसां वैराग्यादिचतुष्टयम्।।3।।
transliteration:
Svavarṇāśramadharmeṇa tapasā haritoṣaṇāt.
Sādhanaṃ prabhavetpuṃsāṃ vairāgyādicatuṣṭayam..3..
summary_line: The four preliminary qualifications (the means to the attainment of knowledge), such as Vairagya (dispassion) and the like, are acquired by men by propitiating Hari (the Lord), through austerities and the performance of duties pertaining to their social order and stage in life.

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेषु वैराग्यं विषयेष्वनु।
यथैव काकविष्ठायां वैराग्यं तद्धि निर्मलम्।।4।।
text:
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेषु वैराग्यं विषयेष्वनु।
यथैव काकविष्ठायां वैराग्यं तद्धि निर्मलम्।।4।।
transliteration:
Brahmādisthāvarānteṣu vairāgyaṃ viṣayeṣvanu.
Yathaiva kākaviṣṭhāyāṃ vairāgyaṃ taddhi nirmalam..4..
summary_line: The indifference with which one treats the excreta of a crow - such an indifference to all objects of enjoyment from the realm of Brahma to this world (in view of their perishable nature), is verily called pure Vairagya.

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
नित्यमात्मस्वरूपं हि दृश्यं तद्विपरीतगम्।
एवं यो निश्चयः सम्यग्विवेको वस्तुनः स वै।।5।।
text:
नित्यमात्मस्वरूपं हि दृश्यं तद्विपरीतगम्।
एवं यो निश्चयः सम्यग्विवेको वस्तुनः स वै।।5।।
transliteration:
Nityamātmasvarūpaṃ hi dṛśyaṃ tadviparītagam.
Evaṃ yo niścayaḥ samyagviveko vastunaḥ sa vai..5..
summary_line: Atman (the seer) in itself is alone permanent, the seen is opposed to it (ie., transient) - such a settled conviction is truly known as discrimination.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Atman (the seer) in itself is alone permanent, the seen is opposed to it (ie., transient) - such a settled conviction is truly known as discrimination.

sanskrit_shloka:
सदैव वासनात्यागः शमोऽयमिति शब्दितः।
निग्रहो बाह्यवृत्तीनां दम इत्यभिधीयते।।6।।
text:
सदैव वासनात्यागः शमोऽयमिति शब्दितः।
निग्रहो बाह्यवृत्तीनां दम इत्यभिधीयते।।6।।
transliteration:
Sadaiva vāsanātyāgaḥ śamo'yamiti śabditaḥ.
Nigraho bāhyavṛttīnāṃ dama ityabhidhīyate..6..
summary_line: Abandonment of desires at all times is called Shama and restraint of the external functions of the organs is called Dama.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Abandonment of desires at all times is called Shama and restraint of the external functions of the organs is called Dama.

sanskrit_shloka:
विषयेभ्यः परावृत्तिः परमोपरतिर्हि सा।
सहनं सर्वदुःखानां तितिक्षा सा शुभा मता।।7।।
text:
विषयेभ्यः परावृत्तिः परमोपरतिर्हि सा।
सहनं सर्वदुःखानां तितिक्षा सा शुभा मता।।7।।
transliteration:
Viṣayebhyaḥ parāvṛttiḥ paramoparatirhi sā.
Sahanaṃ sarvaduḥkhānāṃ titikṣā sā śubhā matā..7..
summary_line: Turning away completely from all sense-objects is the height of Uparati, and patient endurance of all sorrow or pain is known as Titiksha which is conducive to happiness.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Turning away completely from all sense-objects is the height of Uparati, and patient endurance of all sorrow or pain is known as Titiksha which is conducive to happiness.

sanskrit_shloka:
निगमाचार्यवाक्येषु भक्तिः श्रद्धेति विश्रुता।
चित्तैकाग्र्यं तु सल्लक्ष्ये समाधानमिति स्मृतम्।।8।।
text:
निगमाचार्यवाक्येषु भक्तिः श्रद्धेति विश्रुता।
चित्तैकाग्र्यं तु सल्लक्ष्ये समाधानमिति स्मृतम्।।8।।
transliteration:
Nigamācāryavākyeṣu bhaktiḥ śraddheti viśrutā.
Cittaikāgryaṃ tu sallakṣye samādhānamiti smṛtam..8..
summary_line: Implicit faith in the words of the Vedas and the teachers (who interpret them) is known as Shraddha, and concentration of the mind on the only object Sat (i.e., Brahman) is regarded as Samadhana.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Implicit faith in the words of the Vedas and the teachers (who interpret them) is known as Shraddha, and concentration of the mind on the only object Sat (i.e., Brahman) is regarded as Samadhana.

sanskrit_shloka:
संसारबन्धनिर्मुक्तिः कथं स्यान्मे दयानिधे।
इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिर्वक्तव्या सा मुमुक्षुता।।9।।
text:
संसारबन्धनिर्मुक्तिः कथं स्यान्मे दयानिधे।
इति या सुदृढा बुद्धिर्वक्तव्या सा मुमुक्षुता।।9।।
transliteration:
Saṃsārabandhanirmuktiḥ kathaṃ syānme dayānidhe.
Iti yā sudṛḍhā buddhirvaktavyā sā mumukṣutā..9..
summary_line: When and how shall I, O Lord, be free from the bonds of this world (i.e., births and deaths) - such a burning desire is called Mumukshuta.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: When and how shall I, O Lord, be free from the bonds of this world (i.e., births and deaths) - such a burning desire is called Mumukshuta.

sanskrit_shloka:
उक्तसाधनयुक्तेन विचारः पुरुषेण हि।
कर्तव्यो ज्ञानसिद्ध्यर्थमात्मनः शुभमिच्छता।।10।।
text:
उक्तसाधनयुक्तेन विचारः पुरुषेण हि।
कर्तव्यो ज्ञानसिद्ध्यर्थमात्मनः शुभमिच्छता।।10।।
transliteration:
Uktasādhanayuktena vicāraḥ puruṣeṇa hi.
Kartavyo jñānasiddhyarthamātmanaḥ śubhamicchatā..10..
summary_line: Only that person who is in possession of the said qualification (as means to Knowledge) should constantly reflect with a view to attaining Knowledge, desiring his own good.

sanskrit_shloka:
नोत्पद्यते विना ज्ञानं विचारेणान्यसाधनैः।
यथा पदार्थभानं हि प्रकाशेन विना क्वचित्।।11।।
text:
नोत्पद्यते विना ज्ञानं विचारेणान्यसाधनैः।
यथा पदार्थभानं हि प्रकाशेन विना क्वचित्।।11।।
transliteration:
Notpadyate vinā jñānaṃ vicāreṇānyasādhanaiḥ.
Yathā padārthabhānaṃ hi prakāśena vinā kvacit..11..
summary_line: Knowledge is not brought about by any other means than Vichara, just as an object is nowhere perceived (seen) without the help of light.

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
कोऽहं कथमिदं जातं को वा कर्तास्य विद्यते।
उपादानं किमस्तीह विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।12।।
text:
कोऽहं कथमिदं जातं को वा कर्तास्य विद्यते।
उपादानं किमस्तीह विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।12।।
transliteration:
Ko'haṃ kathamidaṃ jātaṃ ko vā kartāsya vidyate.
Upādānaṃ kimastīha vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..12..
summary_line: Who am I ? How is this (world) created ? Who is its creator ? Of what material is this (world) made ? This is the way of that Vichara (enquiry).

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Who am I ? How is this (world) created ? Who is its creator ? Of what material is this (world) made ? This is the way of that Vichara (enquiry).

sanskrit_shloka:
नाहं भूतगणो देहो नाहं चाक्षगणस्तथा।
एतद्विलक्षणः कश्चिद्विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।13।।
text:
नाहं भूतगणो देहो नाहं चाक्षगणस्तथा।
एतद्विलक्षणः कश्चिद्विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।13।।
transliteration:
Nāhaṃ bhūtagaṇo deho nāhaṃ cākṣagaṇastathā.
Etadvilakṣaṇaḥ kaścidvicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..13..
summary_line: I am neither the body, a combination of the (five) elements (of matter), nor am I an aggregate of the senses; I am something different from these. This is the way of that Vichara.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: I am neither the body, a combination of the (five) elements (of matter), nor am I an aggregate of the senses; I am something different from these. This is the way of that Vichara.

sanskrit_shloka:
अज्ञानप्रभवं सर्वं ज्ञानेन प्रविलीयते।
संकल्पो विविधः कर्ता विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।14।।
text:
अज्ञानप्रभवं सर्वं ज्ञानेन प्रविलीयते।
संकल्पो विविधः कर्ता विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।14।।
transliteration:
Ajñānaprabhavaṃ sarvaṃ jñānena pravilīyate.
Saṃkalpo vividhaḥ kartā vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..14..
summary_line: Everything is produced by ignorance, and dissolves in the wake of Knowledge. The various thoughts (modifications of Antahkarana) must be the creator. Such is this Vichara.

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Everything is produced by ignorance, and dissolves in the wake of Knowledge. The various thoughts (modifications of Antahkarana) must be the creator. Such is this Vichara.

sanskrit_shloka:
एतयोर्यदुपादानमेकं सूक्ष्मं सदव्ययम्।
यथैव मृद्धटादीनां विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।15।।
text:
एतयोर्यदुपादानमेकं सूक्ष्मं सदव्ययम्।
यथैव मृद्धटादीनां विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।15।।
transliteration:
Etayoryadupādānamekaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sadavyayam.
Yathaiva mṛddhaṭādīnāṃ vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..15..
summary_line: The material (cause) of these two (i.e., ignorance and thought) is the One (without a second), subtle (not apprehended by the senses) and unchanging Sat (Existence), just as the earth is the material (cause) of the pot and the like. This is the way of that Vichara.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहमेकोऽपि सूक्ष्मश्च ज्ञाता साक्षी सदव्ययः।
तदहं नात्र संदेहो विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।16।।
text:
अहमेकोऽपि सूक्ष्मश्च ज्ञाता साक्षी सदव्ययः।
तदहं नात्र संदेहो विचारः सोऽयमीदृशः।।16।।
transliteration:
Ahameko'pi sūkṣmaśca jñātā sākṣī sadavyayaḥ.
Tadahaṃ nātra saṃdeho vicāraḥ so'yamīdṛśaḥ..16..
summary_line: As I am also the One, the Subtle, the Knower, the Witness, the Ever-Existent, and the Unchanging, so there is no doubt that I am "That" (i.e., Brahman). Such is this enquiry.

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मा विनिष्कलो ह्येको देहो बहुभिरावृतः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।17।।
text:
आत्मा विनिष्कलो ह्येको देहो बहुभिरावृतः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।17।।
transliteration:
Ātmā viniṣkalo hyeko deho bahubhirāvṛtaḥ.
Tayoraikyaṃ prapaśyanti kimajñānamataḥ param..17..
summary_line: Atman is verily one and without parts, whereas the body consists of many parts; and yet the people see (confound) these two as one ! What else can be called ignorance but this ?

translations.author: Traditional Translation
translations.text: Atman is verily one and without parts, whereas the body consists of many parts; and yet the people see (confound) these two as one ! What else can be called ignorance but this ?

sanskrit_shloka:
आत्मा नियामकश्चान्तर्देहो नियम्यबाह्यकः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।18।।
text:
आत्मा नियामकश्चान्तर्देहो नियम्यबाह्यकः।
तयोरैक्यं प्रपश्यन्ति किमज्ञानमतः परम्।।18।।
transliteration:

sanskrit_shloka:
तत्रैव च समाख्यातः स्वयंज्योतिर्हि पूरुषः।
जडः परप्रकाश्योऽयं कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।37।।
text:
तत्रैव च समाख्यातः स्वयंज्योतिर्हि पूरुषः।
जडः परप्रकाश्योऽयं कथं स्याद्देहकः पुमान्।।37।।
transliteration:
Tatraiva ca samākhyātaḥ svayaṃjyotirhi pūruṣaḥ.
Jaḍaḥ paraprakāśyo'yaṃ kathaṃ syāddehakaḥ pumān..37..
summary_line: There again it is clearly stated that "the Purusha is self-illumined". So how can the body which is inert (insentient) and illumined by an external agent be the Purusha ?

प्रोक्तोऽपि कर्मकाण्डेन ह्यात्मा देहाद्विलक्षणः।
नित्यश्च तत्फलं भुङ्क्ते देहपातादनन्तरम्।।38।।
text:
प्रोक्तोऽपि कर्मकाण्डेन ह्यात्मा देहाद्विलक्षणः।
नित्यश्च तत्फलं भुङ्क्ते देहपातादनन्तरम्।।38।।
transliteration:
Prokto'pi karmakāṇḍena hyātmā dehādvilakṣaṇaḥ.
Nityaśca tatphalaṃ bhuṅkte dehapātādanantaram..38..
summary_line: Moreover, the Karma-kanda also declares that the Atman is different from the body and permanent, as it endures even after the fall of the body and reaps the fruits of actions (done in this life).

sanskrit_shloka:
लिङ्गं चानेकसंयुक्तं चलं दृश्यं विकारि च।
अव्यापकमसद्रूपं तत्कथं स्यात्पुमानयम्।।39।।
text:
लिङ्गं चानेकसंयुक्तं चलं दृश्यं विकारि च।
अव्यापकमसद्रूपं तत्कथं स्यात्पुमानयम्।।39।।
transliteration:
Liṅgaṃ cānekasaṃyuktaṃ calaṃ dṛśyaṃ vikāri ca.
Avyāpakamasadrūpaṃ tatkathaṃ syātpumānayam..39..
summary_line: Even the subtle body consists of many parts and is unstable. It is also an object of perception, is changeable, limited and non-existent by nature. So how can this be the Purusha?

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
एवं देहद्वयादन्य आत्मा पुरुष ईश्वरः।
सर्वात्मा सर्वरूपश्च सर्वातीतोऽहमव्ययः।।40।।
text:
एवं देहद्वयादन्य आत्मा पुरुष ईश्वरः।
सर्वात्मा सर्वरूपश्च सर्वातीतोऽहमव्ययः।।40।।
transliteration:
Evaṃ dehadvayādanya ātmā puruṣa īśvaraḥ.
Sarvātmā sarvarūpaśca sarvātīto'hamavyayaḥ..40..
summary_line: The immutable Atman, the substratum of the ego, is thus different from these two bodies, and is the Purusha, the Ishwara (the Lord of all), the Self of all; It is present in every form and yet transcends them all.

sanskrit_shloka:
इत्यात्मदेहभानेन प्रपञ्चस्यैव सत्यता।
यथोक्ता तर्कशास्त्रेण ततः किं पुरुषार्थता।।41।।
text:
इत्यात्मदेहभानेन प्रपञ्चस्यैव सत्यता।
यथोक्ता तर्कशास्त्रेण ततः किं पुरुषार्थता।।41।।
transliteration:
Ityātmadehabhānena prapañcasyaiva satyatā.
Yathoktā tarkaśāstreṇa tataḥ kiṃ puruṣārthatā..41..
summary_line: Thus the enunciation of the difference between the Atman and the body has (indirectly) asserted, indeed, after the manner of the Tarkashastra, the reality of the phenomenal world. But what end of human life is served thereby ?

sanskrit_shloka:
इत्यात्मदेहभेदेन देहात्मत्वं निवारितम्।
इदानीं देहभेदस्य ह्यसत्त्वं स्फुटमुच्यते।।42।।
text:
इत्यात्मदेहभेदेन देहात्मत्वं निवारितम्।
इदानीं देहभेदस्य ह्यसत्त्वं स्फुटमुच्यते।।42।।
transliteration:
Ityātmadehabhedena dehātmatvaṃ nivāritam.
Idānīṃ dehabhedasya hyasattvaṃ sphuṭamucyate..42..
summary_line: Thus the view that the body is the Atman has been denounced by the enunciation of the difference between the Atman and the body. Now is clearly stated the unreality of the difference between the two.

sanskrit_shloka:
चैतन्यस्यैकरूपत्वाद्भेदो युक्तो न कर्हिचित्।
जीवत्वं च मृषा ज्ञेयं रज्ज्वां सर्पग्रहो यथा।।43।।
text:
चैतन्यस्यैकरूपत्वाद्भेदो युक्तो न कर्हिचित्।
जीवत्वं च मृषा ज्ञेयं रज्ज्वां सर्पग्रहो यथा।।43।।
transliteration:
Caitanyasyaikarūpatvādbhedo yukto na karhicit.
Jīvatvaṃ ca mṛṣā jñeyaṃ rajjvāṃ sarpagraho yathā..43..
summary_line: No division in Consciousness is admissible at any time as it is always one and the same. Even the individuality of the Jiva must be known as false, like the delusion of a snake in a rope.

sanskrit_shloka:
रज्ज्वज्ञानात्क्षणेनैव यद्वद्रज्जुर्हि सर्पिणी।
भाति तद्वच्चितिः साक्षाद्विश्वाकारेण केवला।।44।।
text:
रज्ज्वज्ञानात्क्षणेनैव यद्वद्रज्जुर्हि सर्पिणी।
भाति तद्वच्चितिः साक्षाद्विश्वाकारेण केवला।।44।।
transliteration:
Rajjvajñānātkṣaṇenaiva yadvadrajjurhi sarpiṇī.
Bhāti tadvaccitiḥ sākṣādviśvākāreṇa kevalā..44..
summary_line: As through the ignorance of the real nature of the rope the very rope appears in an instant as a snake, so also does pure Consciousness appear in the form of the phenomenal universe without undergoing any change.

sanskrit_shloka:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य ब्रह्मणोऽन्यन्न विद्यते।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रपञ्चोऽयं ब्रह्मैवास्ति न चेतरत्।।45।।
text:
उपादानं प्रपञ्चस्य ब्रह्मणोऽन्यन्न विद्यते।
तस्मात्सर्वप्रपञ्चोऽयं ब्रह्मैवास्ति न चेतरत्।।45।।
transliteration:
Upādānaṃ prapañcasya brahmaṇo'nyanna vidyate.
Tasmātsarvaprapañco'yaṃ brahmaivāsti na cetarat..45..
summary_line: There exists no other material cause of this phenomenal universe except Brahman. Hence this whole universe is but Brahman and nothing else.

translations.author: Traditional Translation

sanskrit_shloka:
व्याप्यव्यापकता मिथ्या सर्वमात्मेति शासनात्।
इति ज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे भेदस्यावसरः कुतः।।46।।
text:
व्याप्यव्यापकता मिथ्या सर्वमात्मेति शासनात्।
इति ज्ञाते परे तत्त्वे भेदस्यावसरः कुतः।।46।।
transliteration:
Vyāpyavyāpakatā mithyā sarvamātmeti śāsanāt.
Iti jñāte pare tattve bhedasyāvasaraḥ kutaḥ..46..
summary_line: From such declaration (of the Shruti) as "All this is Atman", it follows that the idea of the pervaded and the pervading is illusory. This supreme truth being realized, where is the room for any distinction between the cause and the effect ?

sanskrit_shloka:
श्रुत्या निवारितं नूनं नानात्वं स्वमुखेन हि।
कथं भासो भवेदन्यः स्थिते चाद्वयकारणे।।47।।
text:
श्रुत्या निवारितं नूनं नानात्वं स्वमुखेन हि।
कथं भासो भवेदन्यः स्थिते चाद्वयकारणे।।47।।
transliteration:
Śrutyā nivāritaṃ nūnaṃ nānātvaṃ svamukhena hi.
Kathaṃ bhāso bhavedanyaḥ sthite cādvayakāraṇe..47..
summary_line: Certainly the Shruti has directly denied manifoldness in Brahman. The non-dual cause being an established fact, how could the phenomenal universe be different from It ?

sanskrit_shloka:
दोषोऽपि विहितः श्रुत्या मृत्योर्मृत्युं स गच्छति।
इह पश्यति नानात्वं मायया वञ्चितो नरः।।48।।
text:
दोषोऽपि विहितः श्रुत्या मृत्योर्मृत्युं स गच्छति।
इह पश्यति नानात्वं मायया वञ्चितो नरः।।48।।
transliteration:
Doṣo'pi vihitaḥ śrutyā mṛtyormṛtyuṃ sa gacchati.
Iha paśyati nānātvaṃ māyayā vañcito naraḥ..48..
summary_line: Moreover, the Shruti has condemned (the belief in variety) in the words, "The person who", being deceived by Maya, "sees variety in this (Brahman), goes from death to death".

sanskrit_shloka:
ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि जायन्ते परमात्मनः।
तस्मादेतानि ब्रह्मैव भवन्तीत्यवधारयेत्।।49।।
text:
ब्रह्मणः सर्वभूतानि जायन्ते परमात्मनः।
तस्मादेतानि ब्रह्मैव भवन्तीत्यवधारयेत्।।49।।

Brahmaṇaḥ sarvabhūtāni jāyante paramātmanaḥ.
Tasmādetāni brahmaiva bhavantītyavadhārayet..49..
summary_line: Inasmuch as all beings are born of Brahman, the supreme Atman, they must be understood to be verily Brahman.

कर्माण्यपि समग्राणि बिभर्तीति श्रुतिर्जगौ।।50।।
text:
ब्रह्मैव सर्वनामानि रूपाणि विविधानि च।
कर्माण्यपि समग्राणि बिभर्तीति श्रुतिर्जगौ।।50।।

summary_line: The Shruti has clearly declared that Brahman alone is the substratum of all varieties of names, forms and actions.
